INDEPENDENT REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (R02) — INIT-C-PREP-R01v1 starter structures
Same reviewer as source-review.md (R01). Bounded scope: the test delta and the closure of conditions 5.1/5.2/5.3 only. I executed nothing — no Godot, no Python, no git, no hashing. Every execution figure below is quoted from the supplied records. Production module (462cda6a…) and metadata harness (daf155ca…) are unchanged from the hashes I approved in R01 and were NOT re-audited; the 620-value authored-fixture audit from R01 stands and is not repeated.

=========================================================
1. VERDICT
=========================================================
APPROVE THE TEST DELTA. No new must-fix. No correctness, safety or allocation defect introduced.

Conditions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 are SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED on the evidence supplied. The residual gates are exactly the ones Astra already holds open and which I do not presume: (a) the concurrent full regression against THIS test file, (b) exact-head CI, (c) committed-blob identity at PR. My R01 approval stands, now with its reference-loading condition met by implementation rather than waiver.

=========================================================
2. CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR REVIEW
=========================================================
R01 §7 stated that `_neighbour_candidates()` "returns a <=4-element Array per furniture row". That bound is WRONG AS STATED — it is the bound for a single-tile footprint only. Astra's correction is right: the helper unions the unoccupied, unblocked orthogonal neighbours of EVERY footprint tile, so a two-tile interior footprint can yield up to 6 distinct adjacent cells (2 above, 2 below, 1 left, 1 right for a 1x2 strip). The correct general statements are: for an n-tile straight strip the tight bound is 2n+2; absolutely, the result is bounded by the distinct interior tiles adjacent to the footprint and therefore by INTERIOR_TILE_COUNT − footprint_count (<= 79); and the whole arena is independently bounded by CANDIDATE_ROW_COUNT = 132 with the tail pinned to -1.
This correction changes NO conclusion: the 2480-byte payload, the 4960-byte two-Plan peak, the "bounded graph scratch over 80 tiles and 8 edges" compliance and the "no hot-path allocation" finding are all unaffected, because the helper is cold-path, called 31 times, and bounded by the 80-tile interior either way. I record the error plainly rather than quietly restating the bound.

=========================================================
3. THE TEST DELTA — WHAT I VERIFIED
=========================================================
Reviewed file: candidate-test_starter_structures.gd, sha e972ab6f…, which is the hash recorded in BOTH the focused execution record and the installed-identity record. Two patches sit in the evidence directory (review-test-followup.patch, then review-test-completion.patch, which splits the single combined reference test into four guarded tests and types one loop counter); the final file hash is the authority and is correctly pinned in the run records.

3.1 Frozen-reference loading (item 1) — IMPLEMENTED CORRECTLY, NOT WAIVED.
Four new tests load `res://../docs/validation/evidence/starter-integration-planning-2026-09-20/layout-reference.json` and cross-check it against the literal oracle. I assessed the loading semantics line by line:
- Guards are complete and fail LOUDLY rather than skipping: `_load_layout_reference()` checks `FileAccess.file_exists`, non-empty read, and `is Dictionary`, recording `fail()` and returning `{}` on each miss; `_typed_array()` checks key presence AND that the value is actually an Array before returning it. No unguarded subscript of a missing or wrong-typed key exists anywhere in the new code.
- NO VACUOUS-METHOD RISK. I traced every guard path in all four tests: each one always reaches at least one `assert_equal` (or records a `fail()`, which also increments the assertion counter). The runner's per-method "made no assertions" guard therefore cannot be tripped by a degraded-but-passing path, and a missing/corrupt fixture produces explicit failures in all four tests rather than a silent pass.
- `_int_or_fail()` accepts a genuine `int` OR an integral `float` and FAILS on anything else, including a fractional float, a bool or a String. This is the right call and removes a real version-dependence hazard: Godot's JSON parser has historically returned numbers as float, and a naive `int(...)` cast would have silently coerced a malformed value into a matching integer. Note the deliberate design: a malformed element records a failure and returns 0, so even though 0 is a legal tile value, the failure is already banked and cannot be swallowed by a subsequent accidental match.
- Coverage actually achieved against the JSON: all 8 diagram rows; all 31 `floor_furniture` rows (symbol→key, origin, room, footprint, candidate_walk_tiles); the 7 partitions plus the door, merged and sorted by tile_a into 8 triples with kind; `exit_interior_tile`; `walk_tiles` == `reachable_walk_tiles`, count 47, and equality with this suite's OWN footprint-derived complement of the 80 interior tiles (`_oracle_walk_tiles()`), which is a genuinely independent reconstruction rather than a restatement.
- Edge merge is deterministic: the eight tile_a values are distinct, so `sort_custom` yields a total order; a non-pair partition entry or a non-pair door both produce a `fail()` AND a size mismatch.

3.2 What the frozen reference DOES NOT carry, and therefore what remains literal-only.
The JSON contains no buildings, no room runs/offsets/counts, no header values, and no exit WALL or EXTERIOR globals, and no bed-ordinal order. Those remain contract-prose literals. The suite header now says this explicitly, which is honest and correct. The compensating evidence for that remainder is my R01 independent re-derivation (building origins/footprints and pairwise disjointness; the four room runs summing to 80 with ascending row-major order; the three-part exit including wall (64,68) inside the hall footprint and exterior (64,69) outside all seven; header 1/51/33/47). Condition 5.3 is therefore closed by EXECUTABLE means for the furniture/edge/exit-interior/diagram/walk half and by prose+review for the other half — an accurate characterisation that should not be overstated in the acceptance record.
One residual provenance limit, stated once: the chain now verified is literals ↔ layout-reference.json. The link layout-reference.json ↔ GDD remains attested by the `gdd_sha256` recorded inside that artifact and is not re-verified by this suite (the GDD is outside this packet). That is appropriate scope, not a defect.

3.3 Non-aliasing witness (item 2) — CLOSES MY R01 MEDIUM-1.
`test_same_producer_two_outputs_do_not_alias` prepares A and B from the SAME producer, snapshots B, dirties index 0 of all ten of A's arrays, asserts all ten of B's arrays unchanged, then does the reverse. This is exactly the hazard I flagged. It is stronger than a pure COW check: if the producer ever retained its staged Plan and republished the same buffers into a second output, A and B would share storage and this test would fail. The `_dirty_all_arrays()` helper is typed and documented.

3.4 The other four requested witnesses — ALL CORRECT.
- Wall-interior witness corrected from the exit tile's own global (64,67) to the ADJACENT interior global (64,66) = interior-local 65. I verified this now exercises the intended branch: (64,66) IS orthogonally adjacent to the exit's (64,67), so the adjacency gate passes and refusal comes from `_global_to_local(wall) != -1`, i.e. "the wall tile is still interior". The old case was rejected by adjacency (same tile) and never reached that branch. This precisely closes my R01 LOW-3. Astra's accompanying note — that the "wall not inside any building footprint" branch stays defensive and unexercised because the hall footprint covers the entire wall band, with no branch-coverage claim made — is accurate and appropriately hedged.
- `walk_tile_count` header drift (46) now reaches STARTER_WALK_DISCONNECTED via `_flood_reachable`'s declared-vs-expected comparison. Both walk cases moved into the case matrix, so they now also inherit the purity and repeated-determinism assertions that the former standalone test lacked — a real strengthening beyond what was asked.
- Explicit out-of-range candidate value (2147483647 at used slot 0) now sits alongside the coherently-compacted missing-neighbour case. Worth stating why this is safe rather than merely passing: the validator only ever COMPARES stored candidate values against its own recomputed set and never uses a stored value as an index, so an extreme stored value cannot produce an unsafe access — this test documents that property.
- Room-ordinal tautology replaced with a typed loop reading the ACTUAL stored protected type ids for ordinals 1..3 (2, 4, 6 vs ordinals 1, 2, 3). Closes my R01 LOW-4.

3.5 ARITHMETIC CORROBORATION OF THE FOCUSED RECORD (an independent check I can make without executing).
The focused record reports 35 tests / 3674 assertions / 0 failures, versus the prior 30 / 3360. I reconstructed the deltas from the delivered source: +5 tests (4 reference + 1 non-aliasing; the walk test stays one method). Assertions: each matrix case contributes 22 (code + 10-array snapshot + repeat code + 10-array snapshot). Walk test 1→44 = +43; new candidate case = +22; room ordinals 7→9 = +2; non-aliasing = 2+10+10 = +22; reference tests = 9 (diagram) + 187 (31 rows x 6 + size) + 25 (8 edges x 3 + size) + 4 (exit/walk) = +225. Total +314, and 3360 + 314 = 3674 EXACTLY. The reported counts are therefore arithmetically consistent with this exact source file, which independently corroborates that the recorded run was against sha e972ab6f… rather than some other state. I still make no claim that the suite passes on my machine.

=========================================================
4. CONDITION-BY-CONDITION ASSESSMENT
=========================================================
4.1 — SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED. `integrated-static-checks.json` shows all 17 specification checks at exit 0 AFTER installation, including the three source-scanning ones I flagged: `validate_save_registry_handoff.py --source-root .`, `generate_canonical_state_table.py --check`, `audit_registry_capacities.py --check`, plus `generate_component_columns_schema.py --check` and `test_component_columns_schema.py`.
The decisive detail is one I checked rather than assumed: the coverage line reports the IDENTICAL census before and after installation — "83 modules, 390 rows, 684 packed columns" and "554 persisted packed fields" in both runs. Installing a new file under `godot/scripts/core/` with ten `PackedInt32Array` members therefore added zero counted packed columns, which is consistent with those members living inside the inner `Plan` class rather than at module level. Combined with the fact that `docs/persistence_state_registry.md` now carries a `### godot/scripts/core/starter_structures.gd` heading, both halves of the checker's contract are satisfied: the store has a row, and it declares no packed columns to mismatch. My R01 concern is resolved empirically.
I also verified there is no hidden inconsistency in the unchanged `decision_numbers.py` count of 177: decision 0184 existed in both runs, and appending the "Independent source review disposition" section (hash 72ff6e66 → 028b81f1) changes the record's content, not the record COUNT.
The new registry row is accurate to the module as I audited it: ten caller-owned arrays, 2480 logical bytes, 4960 caller-plus-staged bound, COW publication on success, prior output preserved on refusal, `last_refusal` transient, category 3, no save section, and explicit non-claims for body fit, topology publication, room validity, heat, contacts and container admission. It correctly does not present native overhead as measured.
RESIDUAL: these runs are local. Exact-head CI on the committed tree remains the gate, as Astra states.

4.2 — SUBSTANTIALLY CLOSED. `integrated-candidate-review-followup.json` records `tools/test_starter_structures_metadata.py` at daf155ca… — byte-identical to the reviewed evidence candidate — so `ROOT = parents[1]` resolves correctly and the reviewed workflow step `python3 tools/test_starter_structures_metadata.py` is valid. `metadata-hardened.log` independently corroborates installation by resolving the module as "production module (already installed)" at `godot/scripts/core/starter_structures.gd` with sha 462cda6a…, equal to the evidence copy.
TRANSPARENCY NOTE: the disposition cites `integrated-candidate-identity.json`, which is NOT in this packet; I could not read it and did not rely on it. My conclusion rests only on the two records above.
RESIDUAL: commit-blob identity recheck before PR, which Astra already holds.

4.3 — CLOSED BY IMPLEMENTATION, NOT WAIVER, and I endorse that choice as the better outcome. Assessment in §3.1–3.2, including the honest boundary of what the JSON can and cannot pin. I withdraw my R01 suggestion that a waiver would have been an acceptable disposition; an executable check is strictly stronger and the `res://../docs` pattern makes it practical.

=========================================================
5. ASTRA'S DISPOSITION OF MY NON-BLOCKING ITEMS
=========================================================
MEDIUM-1 — Implemented. Accepted, withdrawn.
MEDIUM-2 (30-line function rule) — ACCEPTED, WITHDRAWN. ADR 0184 now records a narrow, module-scoped style exception for the existing long sequential validation/fill/exact-match functions, trivial column accessors without separate docstrings, and inferred integer loop counters, while explicitly NOT relaxing typed authoritative storage, refusal ordering, bounds checks, hot-path rules or any functional acceptance criterion, and requiring new helpers to stay typed, documented and short. That is the authority that owns the rule, recording the exception in the place AGENTS.md requires, with the right carve-outs. I verified the delivered new helpers do comply (typed signatures, docstrings, all short, typed loop counters). One caution for the record: this exception is module-scoped to a cold preparation module and should not be cited as precedent for an owner or hot-path module.
MEDIUM-3 (use `Catalog.verify_compiled_enum`) — ASTRA IS RIGHT AND MY RECOMMENDATION WAS WRONG. I verified it in the supplied source: `verify_compiled_enum()` compares `int(table[key]) != expected`, and `int("29") == 29`, so a String-typed catalog id would PASS that verifier. The module's `_is_ascending_key_id_map()` instead requires `typeof(key) == TYPE_STRING` and `typeof(dict[key]) == TYPE_INT` and refuses outright. Two currently-passing fault witnesses depend on exactly that strictness — `building-catalog-integer-type` (`workshop` → "29") and `furniture-catalog-integer-type` (`shelf` → "8"), both recorded as caught with STARTER_SOURCE_METADATA in metadata-hardened.log. A direct substitution would silently regress both. I withdraw MEDIUM-3 entirely; the local strict helper is the correct implementation and the apparent DRY duplication is justified by a real semantic difference that should stay documented where it is.
LOW-1 (hall-footprint drift attributed to ROOM_LAYOUT) — Accepted as retained. With an incompatible hall extent the interior genuinely cannot be established, so the attribution is deterministic and defensible. Withdrawn as a finding; retained as a behaviour note for the future materializer.
LOW-2, LOW-3, LOW-4 — Witnesses added/corrected and verified in §3.4. Withdrawn.
LOW-5 — Covered by the ADR exception; new code complies. Withdrawn.
LOW-6 (redundant metadata double-scan, repeated ownership recomputation) — Accepted as retained: bounded, cold, and no hot-path or native-memory claim is made either way. Withdrawn as actionable.
LOW-7 (rotated pivot semantics) — Correctly deferred to the future materializer and now recorded in ADR 0184; all authored rows are rotation 0 and the extent calculation is correct for its bounded role. Withdrawn.

=========================================================
6. NEW FINDINGS IN THIS DELTA (all LOW, none blocking)
=========================================================
NEW-1 — `layout-reference.json` IS NOW A LOAD-BEARING TEST FIXTURE, NOT MERELY EVIDENCE. The suite reads it at runtime through `res://../docs/...`, so deleting, renaming, archiving or pruning that evidence directory will FAIL the headless suite rather than degrade it. That failure direction is correct and deliberate, but the coupling should be recorded where an evidence-cleanup task would see it (a line in the evidence directory or in the preparation contract). This is the one finding here with real future-breakage potential.
NEW-2 — The suite header docstring names `test_frozen_layout_reference_matches_the_literal_oracle`, a method that DOES NOT EXIST in the delivered file: the completion patch split it into `..._diagram_matches_the_oracle`, `..._furniture_matches_the_oracle`, `..._edges_match_the_oracle` and `..._exit_and_walk_tiles_match_the_oracle`. The substance of the header (reference is loaded and cross-checked; building/room/header values remain contract literals) is accurate; only the method name is stale. Recommend naming the four, or referring to the `test_frozen_layout_reference_*` family.
NEW-3 — The new `### godot/scripts/core/starter_structures.gd` section in `docs/persistence_state_registry.md` uses column headings ("Width | Count | Empty/sentinel | Category | Save section") that diverge from every other section in that document ("Width B | Count | Null / unused | Cat | ARCH-SAVE-002"). The checker accepts it today (exit 0), but the divergence is a maintenance hazard and a trap for any future stricter parser. Cosmetic alignment recommended.
NEW-4 — `sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[0] < b[0])` uses untyped lambda parameters in new test code. The ADR exception covers inferred integer LOOP COUNTERS, not lambda parameters; `func(a: Array, b: Array) -> bool` would comply. Cosmetic, non-blocking.
NEW-5 — Path resolution of `res://../docs/...` is environment-dependent in principle (it escapes the project root and would not resolve inside an exported PCK). It is fine for headless runs, where `--path godot` makes res:// the project directory and `..` reaches the repo root, and the supplied focused record demonstrates it resolved there. It also fails loudly rather than silently if it ever does not. I cannot execute, so I fold confirmation into the existing exact-head CI gate rather than asserting it.

=========================================================
7. THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN (no action)
=========================================================
- No production source change: the module hash is unchanged from R01, and nothing in the delta touches it. No public bypass, no new world owner, no startup wiring, no save-schema claim was introduced by the test work.
- No interaction between the new reference test and the metadata harness's owned clone: `prepare_clone()` copies `godot/` (now including this suite) and symlinks `docs/`, but the generated focus script restricts discovery to the probe suite alone, so the faulted-catalog, autoload-stripped clone never runs this suite. A reader might reasonably worry about that; it does not occur.
- The harness's fail-closed credit rule is unchanged and still cannot credit a parse/runtime/engine error as a semantic refusal.
- The new reference tests cannot mask a transcription error in the direction that matters: if a literal and the JSON disagree, the test fails. They cannot catch an error present identically in both, which is why the frozen artifact's own GDD provenance (§3.2) and my R01 re-derivation remain the outer checks.
- `integrated-candidate-review-followup.json` is honest that the earlier 5029/525772 full-suite record applies to the PRIOR 30-test suite and that a new full run is pending. I endorse that framing and do not treat the old figure as covering this file.

=========================================================
8. REMAINING CONDITIONS (unchanged in substance; none presumed satisfied)
=========================================================
C1. The concurrent FULL regression against this exact test file (e972ab6f…) must complete and pass. For Astra's cross-check only, and explicitly not a prediction: if nothing else changed, the totals should move by exactly +5 tests and +314 assertions from the 5029/525772 baseline (i.e. 5034/526086) with 0 failures; a different delta would itself be a signal worth investigating. The known baseline shutdown diagnostics (553 ObjectDB instances, 33 resources) remain a separate tracked release issue and are not this packet's defect.
C2. Exact-head CI on the committed tree, covering the full Godot suite, the starter metadata step and the 17 specification checks.
C3. Committed-blob identity between the evidence copies and the installed files (module, suite, focus script, harness) at PR.
These are Astra's gates. Nothing in this review authorises acceptance, application of any source, or any claim that a run occurred.

=========================================================
9. LIMITATIONS OF THIS FOLLOW-UP
=========================================================
- I executed nothing and hashed nothing; all counts are quoted.
- I did not re-audit the unchanged production module or the unchanged metadata harness; R01's findings for those stand at their stated hashes.
- I could not read `integrated-candidate-identity.json` (absent from this packet) and did not rely on it.
- I could not read the source of `state_registry_coverage.py` / `validate_save_registry_handoff.py`; my 5.1 conclusion rests on the identical pre/post-install census figures and the exit-0 record, not on reading the validators.
- `milestones.gd` remains unread (absent from both packets); it is never instantiated by this module, so it cannot affect behaviour here.
- No claim is made about physical access, body fit, room validity, heat, exterior reachability, real contacts, startup, save continuation, native/RSS qualification, or INIT-C/D/E/FP-01 completion. Tile adjacency in this Plan remains authored data only.

=========================================================
10. ONE-LINE DISPOSITION
=========================================================
The test delta correctly and safely implements all five requested witnesses and closes condition 5.3 by genuine frozen-reference loading with complete fail-loud guards and no vacuous-method path; 5.1 and 5.2 are corroborated by the post-installation checks, the unchanged packed-column census, the new cold-derived registry row and the matching harness/module hashes; Astra's rejection of my `verify_compiled_enum` suggestion is correct and my own `<=4` neighbour bound is corrected; the only new findings are LOW (the evidence JSON is now a load-bearing fixture, a stale method name in the suite header, a divergent registry table heading, and one untyped comparator), and acceptance remains gated on the pending full regression, exact-head CI and committed identity.
